Phase 55 plan @ ecf0fec (branch phase/measure-the-loop): docs/phases/measure-the-loop.md + roadmap entry.
Scope: read-only `tagteam report --phase P [--json]` (rounds, change requests, gate bounces/minutes, per-role elapsed turn time from entry ts, start→approve, tokens only where headless usage rows exist, 'not recorded'/'partial' otherwise); `usage --by role|cycle|model|kind` with cost dropped from text (kept in --json); schema v10 usage.model_usage_json from Claude modelUsage (four token fields, bounded); cost removed from cockpit/hub views.
Arbiter rulings already made (2026-09-14): data only from what tagteam stores (no ~/.claude or ~/.codex reads); tagteam grade split to a later phase; report is printed, never written on approval; step 0 effort experiment skipped (reviewer is Codex, interactive).
Review focus (plan § Risks): elapsed-vs-effort labelling, model buckets counting a turn per model, rate-limit 'last signal' only, command name report vs usage --report.
Verification: document checks only for the plan; roadmap check ok (55 phases).

The scope and product choices are sound: keep report separate from usage; elapsed-time labels are sufficient; model buckets may count a turn once per model with the proposed label; rate-limit snapshots must remain last-signal observations. Honor the recorded arbiter rulings (project-owned data only, grade deferred, printed report, no effort experiment). Two measurement/read-path issues need explicit plan revisions before implementation:

1. Correct the token coverage contract for actual stored usage identities and missing token values. The proposed phase+type+round+role match is not a submission identity: headless.snapshot_identity computes target_round=N+1 for a lead responding to round N, but HeadlessEngine._record_usage stores ident.round=N (and ident.phase/type, not target_phase/type). Start commands can likewise target a different cycle. A round-2 lead submission therefore will not match its own usage row under the proposed rule, and may match the wrong turn. Also, _record_usage writes a row even when parsing returned no usage, with all token fields absent; panel lenses and retries produce multiple rows for one cycle turn. Define an evidence-based coverage policy with unknown/ambiguous results where historical rows cannot support exact attribution; do not assert that no rows proves interactive execution, or that a row with null tokens means tokens were recorded. Keep recorded consumption distinct from matched workflow-turn coverage. Add fixtures using the actual incoming-round semantics, null-token rows, retries and panel rows so coverage cannot falsely become complete or exceed its denominator. If future identity capture is needed, make that scope change explicit; do not silently reinterpret old rows.

2. Specify a genuinely read-only path for ordinary report invocation and v9 compatibility. usage_command currently calls db.connect, which creates/migrates unless TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1. cycle.read_rounds/read_status also call db.connect internally, so opening only the report's direct connection read-only does not fulfill 'creates nothing'. Conversely, under TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1, db.connect uses read_only_connect(require_current_schema=True), which rejects v9 after the schema bump before get_usage can treat the new column as absent. Describe the scoped read path that avoids creation/migration across all report readers, preserves DB-first/file-fallback semantics, and permits supported v9 reads without weakening unrelated command guards. Add ordinary-mode report checks on a files-only project and a v9 project (no files/schema changes), plus the promised read-only-mode v9 report/usage checks. Adjust the Files list if shared readers need changes.

Reviewed the plan against cycle.py, db.py, usage.py, headless.py and usage writers. No tests run for this plan review.

Phase 55 plan round 2 @ 396dc28. Both findings addressed in docs/phases/measure-the-loop.md (see "Plan revision log").
1. Coverage: new sections "Stored consumption" and "Turn coverage". Consumption = rows stored under the phase (owed-state identity, labelled as such), null-token and failed rows counted separately, never as recorded tokens. Coverage denominator = lead submissions + reviewer verdicts; each turn is exactly one of matched / matched-no-token-data / unmatched / unknown (sum invariant). Rules: v10 target identity exact; pre-v10 reviewer row N → verdict N, lead row N → submission N+1 (checked against real safe-framework-migration impl rows: lead r1 row after gate bounce ↔ r2 submission); round-1 lead submissions without target rows → unknown; unattributed lead rows shown, not dropped. Retries/panel lenses count one turn; panel verdicts match only panel rows. "Interactive" wording removed. Explicit scope addition: v10 target_phase/type/round columns written by the headless engine (TurnIdentity) and panel; old rows not reinterpreted.
2. Read path: db.connect_for_read = read_only_connect(require_current_schema=False) in both modes (hub_api precedent), None+note on missing/WAL-without-index; keyword-only conn= on cycle.read_status/read_rounds (+ DB helpers), files-only sentinel when no connection so db.connect is never reached; column-tolerant get_usage for v9/older; usage_command uses the same path (stated behaviour change: ordinary usage no longer creates/migrates). db.connect unchanged. Fixtures added: ordinary + read-only on files-only and v9 projects (no .tagteam created; v9 bytes/user_version unchanged), readers unchanged by default, coverage fixtures for incoming-round semantics, start rows, retries, panels, null tokens. Files list adds cycle.py, db.py, panel.py and their tests.
Verification: document checks only (plan).

The read-path revision resolves finding 2: the scoped connection, explicit files-only sentinel, unchanged default readers and v9 compatibility checks are concrete. Separating stored consumption from coverage and adding target identity also resolve the main attribution concern. Two small but necessary corrections remain in the new coverage specification:

1. Fetch target rows independently of stored consumption. The report inputs still specify db.get_usage(conn, phase=phase), which selects usage.phase, but target_phase can differ from that stored phase (the plan explicitly describes cross-phase start commands). A row stored under phase A with target_phase B will never be loaded for report --phase B, so exact v10 coverage fails for that start. Specify a separate target-aware selection (or load and partition rows once), keep consumption filtered by stored phase, and deduplicate rows selected through both identities. Add a fixture with different stored and target PHASES, not only plan/impl types in the same phase: report B matches its first submission, report A retains stored consumption, and the row never matches an unrelated A submission through fallback.

2. Make coverage statuses exhaustive. An attributable row with token data but status nonzero_exit/cancelled/another non-ok outcome fits none of the four definitions: not matched (requires ok), not no-token-data, not unmatched (a row exists), and not unknown (identity is exact). This can happen when a process writes the cycle entry and then fails, or when failed panel rows coexist with a recorded verdict. Define that case explicitly, either with a separate status or by separating token coverage from execution success, and update the sum invariant. Test an attributable turn with only failed token-bearing rows and another with mixed failed token-bearing / ok null-token rows.

These revisions need only clarify the bounded coverage design, not broaden the product scope. The arbiter rulings remain honored. Document review only; no tests run.
